evidence.claim: Scholz said the cabinet discussed energy security and energy supply with Economic Affairs Minister Robert Habeck and Finance Minister Christian Lindner in a constructive atmosphere.
evidence.title: Closed Cabinet meeting at Schloss Meseberg
evidence.excerpt: Scholz said the cabinet discussed energy security and energy supply with Economic Affairs Minister Robert Habeck and Finance Minister Christian Lindner in a constructive atmosphere.
evidence.source_locator: concluding press conference caption and quoted summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct federal-government archive with named participants and contemporaneous summary.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 cabinet coordination on the core economic shock.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz cabinet leadership; this shows he empowered the key economic ministers.
contrary_evidence: Constructive coordination is not the same as proven policy success.
It is an elite-level meeting, not evidence of household-level impact.

evidence.claim: The Bundestag approved the government bill to raise the statutory minimum wage to 12 euro per hour from 1 October 2022, benefiting more than six million people, especially women and workers in eastern Germany.
evidence.title: Der Mindestlohn steigt auf 12 Euro
evidence.excerpt: The Bundestag approved the government bill to raise the statutory minimum wage to 12 euro per hour from 1 October 2022, benefiting more than six million people, especially women and workers in eastern Germany.
evidence.source_locator: press release body and opening paragraph
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry announcement of an enacted policy with direct distributional effects.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level policy under Scholz; implementation was through the federal government and coalition majority.
contrary_evidence: A higher minimum wage can add some wage-cost pressure.
This is a targeted welfare measure, not a broad productivity reform by itself.

evidence.claim: The cabinet approved a child immediate supplement of 20 euro per month and a one-off payment for people on social-security benefits as an early crisis response.
evidence.title: Mehr Unterstützung für Familien mit wenig Geld
evidence.excerpt: The cabinet approved a child immediate supplement of 20 euro per month and a one-off payment for people on social-security benefits as an early crisis response.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary cabinet-policy announcement from the responsible ministry.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level policy under Scholz, aimed at low-income households.
contrary_evidence: It is emergency relief rather than structural anti-poverty reform.
The measure is compensatory, not a permanent earnings increase.

evidence.claim: The OECD said the government acted swiftly to secure energy supply and support households and firms, while noting that the relief measures could be better targeted to limit fiscal costs and that structural reform needs remained large.
evidence.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Germany 2023
evidence.excerpt: The OECD said the government acted swiftly to secure energy supply and support households and firms, while noting that the relief measures could be better targeted to limit fiscal costs and that structural reform needs remained large.
evidence.source_locator: Executive summary, especially the section on the energy crisis
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major independent surveillance report with direct assessment of the German response.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but directly assessing 2022 policy response and outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution under Scholz; this is an external evaluation rather than self-justification.
contrary_evidence: The OECD’s own critique is that the support could have been better targeted.
It frames the 2022 response as necessary but incomplete.

evidence.claim: Average employment in 2022 reached about 45.6 million people, the highest level since German unification, rising by 589,000 from 2021.
evidence.title: Employment in 2022 at highest level since German unification
evidence.excerpt: Average employment in 2022 reached about 45.6 million people, the highest level since German unification, rising by 589,000 from 2021.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary labor-market statistics source for the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Outcome context under Scholz, influenced by earlier labor-market institutions and external conditions as well as policy.
contrary_evidence: Employment strength does not erase the inflation and real-income losses in the same year.
Immigration and prior labor-market trends also helped.

evidence.claim: The Bundesrechnungshof warned that the 200 billion euro WSF energy shield involved significant fiscal and constitutional risks and said the finance ministry tried to exhaust the 2022 borrowing authorization in a way that undercut the debt rule.
evidence.title: Energie-Schutzschirm: Finanzierung zweifelhaft
evidence.excerpt: The Bundesrechnungshof warned that the 200 billion euro WSF energy shield involved significant fiscal and constitutional risks and said the finance ministry tried to exhaust the 2022 borrowing authorization in a way that undercut the debt rule.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and the section describing the financing construction
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent federal audit body with direct criticism of the financing design.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but focused on the 2022 design decision.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level criticism under Scholz; this concerns finance ministry design choices, not merely macro outcomes.
contrary_evidence: This criticism is about financing design, not the purpose of relief itself.
It is retrospective and therefore less direct than contemporaneous reporting.

evidence.claim: ifo researchers estimated the budget effects of the relief packages at about 130 billion euro over three years and argued that broad compensation can crowd out public goods or lead to higher future taxes.
evidence.title: Entlastungspakete, Tankrabatt, Übergewinnabschöpfung: Wie weit kann der Staat uns in Krisen schützen?
evidence.excerpt: ifo researchers estimated the budget effects of the relief packages at about 130 billion euro over three years and argued that broad compensation can crowd out public goods or lead to higher future taxes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Credible applied-economics analysis, though it is a policy essay rather than a government record.
contrary_evidence: The paper critiques scope and financing, not the entire crisis response.
Its estimates are analytical, not a final fiscal audit.

evidence.claim: The federal cabinet approved a four-year monitoring commission staffed by four named scientists, including Andreas Löschel, Veronika Grimm, Anke Weidlich, and Felix Matthes.
evidence.title: Expertenkommission zum Energiewende-Monitoring nimmt in neuer Besetzung mit einer Analyse zum Strommarktdesign ihre Arbeit auf
evidence.excerpt: The federal cabinet approved a four-year monitoring commission staffed by four named scientists, including Andreas Löschel, Veronika Grimm, Anke Weidlich, and Felix Matthes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry press release naming the experts and the cabinet-approved appointment; strong for the fact of professional staffing, weaker for personal Scholz-level direction.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant cabinet-level attribution under the Scholz government; the chancellor's own appointment decision is not separately documented here.
contrary_evidence: The source shows expert staffing, not that Scholz personally selected each member.
It concerns energy-transition monitoring, not every crisis portfolio.

evidence.claim: The government set up the ExpertInnen-Kommission Gas und Wärme on 23 September 2022, then used its proposals to build a 200 billion euro economic shield and gas/heat price brake through mid-2024.
evidence.title: Wirtschaftlicher Abwehrschirm und Gaspreisbremse: mit Entschlossenheit durch die Energiekrise
evidence.excerpt: The government set up the ExpertInnen-Kommission Gas und Wärme on 23 September 2022, then used its proposals to build a 200 billion euro economic shield and gas/heat price brake through mid-2024.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed official ministry report with dates, institutional setup, and implementation architecture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong cabinet-level attribution under Scholz; the report ties the measures to the federal government, though the technical design was commission-led.
contrary_evidence: It shows design and financing, not post-implementation distributional results.
It is a ministry report, so it is stronger on process than independent outcome evaluation.

unresolved_gaps: Direct evidence on internal nuclear-safety alternatives and command-and-control review is still thin.
Internal cabinet deliberations and precise alternative options around the Ukraine response are not visible.
Most policing and complaint-handling evidence is Länder-level, so direct Scholz attribution remains limited.
Direct evidence of 2022 Scholz-led democratic strengthening is thinner than evidence of institutional baseline and judicial constraint.
Direct chancellor-level evidence on personnel selection, correction after failure, and anti-capture choices remains limited.
Post-enactment delivery quality and longer-run durability of the reforms are not fully shown in the 2022 package.
Direct primary evidence on assets, gifts, family benefit, hidden conflicts, or formal self-dealing is missing.
The record remains allegation-heavy rather than adjudication-heavy on deception and obstruction.
Direct evidence on Scholz's personnel selection, correction of underperformers, and internal discipline is thinner than evidence on program design and rollout.
